direction: Use particle-number continuation to bypass the $N=272$ barrier: first delete 20–40 points (mix of highest-contact and random choices), optimise the smaller code aggressively until its maximum is clearly below the record, then grow back one point at a time—insert at the largest hole, anneal only the new point and its 20 nearest neighbours briefly, then LP-polish all points—recording the maximum after each addition. In parallel within the time budget, run the reverse path: add 8–16 dummy points, optimise $N>272$, and prune the points whose removal most reduces the maximum. Return the best true 272-point configuration encountered, since changing $N$ changes the contact topology and hole structure in a way fixed-$N$ basin hopping cannot.

idea: Walker-based basin hopping with multi-point hole surgery and cluster breakup plus balanced-then-sharp softmax annealing before trust-region LP, accepting uphill moves to leave the over-rigid jammed basin.

Build 272 points as eleven left Hurwitz orbits plus an 8-point cross, optimize only the eleven seed quaternions (with optional per-orbit left-right rotations) under annealed softmax repulsion, then break symmetry with noise and finish by full-point annealing and trust-region LP polish.
direction: Try a genuinely different, symmetry-based construction from quaternions instead of starting near the record: identify $\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb H$, generate orbits of seed unit quaternions under left multiplication by the 24 Hurwitz units (and optionally a second seed family under left–right action), choose about eleven 24-point orbits plus a small special orbit to total 272, and optimise only the seed quaternions with a softmax approximation to the maximum cosine. Then break the symmetry slightly, run full 272-point annealing, and LP polish; also try mixtures in which one orbit is rotated by a general unit-quaternion pair before taking the union. The hypothesis is that a high-symmetry orbit packing has a different and possibly better contact graph than the apparently irregular record, and even if its symmetric optimum is worse, symmetry-broken descendants may land in a new basin.

idea: Escape the over-rigid jammed basin with large topology-changing moves and balanced plus hinge objectives that share load uniformly instead of snapping back to the same contacts.

Escape the over-rigid jammed basin with rigidity-aware collective moves from the contact graph's floppy singular modes and NNLS equilibrium stress, then re-polish with annealed softmax and trust-region LP.
direction: Use the rigidity/stress structure of the current contact graph to generate collective escape directions: build tangent bases $B_i\in\mathbb R^{4\times3}$ for each point, assemble the contact rigidity matrix $R$ for pairs within $10^{-7}$ of the maximum, compute its smallest right-singular vectors and, via the LP dual or a nonnegative least-squares stress solve, an equilibrium-stress vector. Move along $\pm$ combinations of the 5–20 floppyest singular modes with step sizes $0.005$–$0.08$ (converted back through $B_i$, retracting to the sphere), including modes weighted to unload the highest-stress contacts, then run a brief annealed softmax phase ($\beta:50\to800$) and LP polish. This tests structured, graph-aware motions that isotropic Gaussian noise almost never samples, and specifically searches for contact-breaking mechanisms of the jammed core.

idea: N-continuation by deleting high-stress core points, annealing the reduced code, then greedily regrowing at LSE-refined spherical holes with periodic full re-annealing.
direction: Grow the code by $N$-continuation instead of perturbing all 272 points at once: delete the 24–40 points with highest contact degree or largest LP dual stress from `best.npy`, anneal and LP-polish the remaining code until its maximum is substantially below $0.89816$, then reinsert points one at a time at greedily optimized spherical holes—found from at least $50{,}000$ random directions followed by local minimisation of $\log\sum_j \exp(60\langle z,x_j\rangle)$—freezing older points briefly after each insertion and fully re-annealing after every 4–8 insertions. Run several deletion sets (highest-degree, spatially clustered, and random) in parallel time slices, because this changes which points occupy the core and can produce a genuinely different final contact graph.

direction: Search exactly symmetric constructions from groups other than the 24-point Hurwitz orbit used previously, keeping the symmetry unbroken throughout the main optimisation: enumerate partitions of 272 into orbit sizes of finite quaternionic groups such as $Q_8$ (8), dicyclic groups (16 or 32), binary tetrahedral (24), and binary octahedral (48), parameterise each orbit by one seed unit quaternion plus independent left and right unit-quaternion rotations, and optimise only those seeds/rotators with Adam on an annealed softmax objective ($\alpha:20\to500$). Include a Hopf–Clifford family $ (\cos\eta\,e^{i\xi_1},\sin\eta\,e^{i\xi_2}) $ with points distributed over a few $\eta$-tori and optimised angular offsets, score every symmetric candidate exactly, and only in the last 20 seconds allow a tiny symmetry-breaking perturbation followed by LP polish.

idea: Force the most dual-stressed contacts apart with a hinge penalty to change topology, then re-anneal and LP-polish, archiving Jaccard-diverse basins.
direction: Perform targeted contact-graph surgery guided by LP duals: solve the usual trust-region LP once, extract dual multipliers for the active pairs to identify the most stressed contacts and highest-degree points, then choose a small set of 5–15 such edges and explicitly force them apart with a temporary hinge penalty $\sum \max(0,0.885-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)^2$ on the selected pairs plus the normal softmax repulsion on all others, allowing the global maximum to rise to about $0.905$ during the move. After this forced topology change, remove the hinge, re-anneal at moderate temperature, LP-polish, and accept the result into a small archive if its contact graph differs materially (e.g. contact-set Jaccard distance $>0.15$ at slack $10^{-6}$) even when its score is up to $2\times10^{-4}$ worse, iterating surgery from archived diverse basins rather than always from the incumbent.

idea: Recombine diverse annealed basins via SO(4)-aligned half-space crossover with hole repair instead of restarting from the record.
direction: Build a diverse population and recombine basins instead of restarting from the record: generate 6–10 independent configurations by softmax annealing from random starts and from randomised Hopf grids, polish each only briefly, then repeatedly take two elite-but-different parents, align them by optimising a global $SO(4)$ rotation (parameterised by a pair of unit quaternions) and a point matching via `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` on pairwise cosines, and form children by taking matched points from parent A in one Hopf half-space or random spatial half-space and from parent B in the complement, resolving near-duplicates by hole insertion. Anneal and LP-polish each child, retain it if it is either better than the incumbent or has a substantially different contact graph, and use the remaining time for a final long LP polish of the best child, falling back to loading `best.npy` if no child beats it.

idea: Antipodal (136 pairs) and Q8-orbit (34 seeds) symmetric global search with softmax manifold descent from many starts, followed by graduated symmetry-breaking noise with re-annealing and sparse trust-region LP locking plus incumbent rescue.
direction: Search a symmetry-constrained global model from scratch, then break the symmetry gradually. First enforce exact antipodality: optimize 136 representatives $y_k\in S^3$ representing pairs $\pm y_k$, minimizing a softmax approximation to $\max_{k<\ell}|\langle y_k,y_\ell\rangle|$ (the relevant maximum for the full 272-point antipodal code), using many random and low-discrepancy starts; also try the stricter quaternionic version with 34 seeds expanded by left multiplication by $Q8=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ to give $34\cdot8=272$ points. Take the best symmetric codes, introduce a symmetry-breaking amplitude $\varepsilon$ that is increased through values such as $0,10^{-4},3\times10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3},10^{-2}$ with re-annealing and LP polish at each stage, and compare against the incumbent; this tests whether the missing ingredient is global antipodal/orbit organization before allowing full asymmetric relaxation.

idea: Break the isostatic trap with Riesz-balanced restarts plus Hopf-torus seeds and degree-equalized basin-hopping with cap-rotations and hole-regrowth before LP locking.
Excise a 12–20 point contact patch around high-degree centers and rebuild the cavity against a frozen exterior before staged unfreezing.
direction: Perform large patch excision and cavity reconstruction instead of deleting isolated points. Choose a high-contact-degree point (degree 8–10), remove it together with its first contact ring and part of the second ring (about 12–20 points total), freeze the remaining points initially, and refill the cavity by optimizing the removed points against the frozen exterior with softmax repulsion at several temperatures and multiple random/hole-based initializations. Then unfreeze in stages—the refilled patch first, then its boundary ring, then all points—followed by LP polish; repeat for many different centers, including patches containing the rattler, and accept a result only if its polished maximum is below the incumbent or its contact graph is substantially different (Jaccard $<0.85$) with maximum within $10^{-5}$, so genuinely new basins are preserved for further polishing.

idea: Jammed active-set nullspace walk with Jaccard-diverse restarts and LP re-locking.
direction: Implement an active-set nullspace walk that deliberately changes the contact topology. From `best.npy`, take all pairs within $10^{-9}$ of the maximum, build their tangent-space Jacobian $A$ (each contact gives $\langle dx_i,x_j\rangle+\langle x_i,dx_j\rangle$, with $\langle dx_i,x_i\rangle=0$), and compute its smallest singular directions by sparse SVD; step along combinations of the lowest 5–20 null/near-null directions, projecting back to $S^3$, using a line search that keeps current contacts from increasing while reducing the slack of selected noncontacts at slack $10^{-5}$–$10^{-3}$. When a new pair reaches the maximum or an old contact can be dropped without first-order increase, rebuild the active set and LP-polish; archive configurations by contact-graph Jaccard distance and continue from diverse ones rather than always from the lowest score. Always retain the unmodified polished best as a fallback.
